“All of a Sudden,” “Clarissa,” “La Gradiva,” “The Invite” and “Tender Loving Care” lead the nominations for the 36th edition of The Gothams with four nods each.
The Gotham Film & Media Institute announced nominations for the 36th edition of The Gothams, singling out 42 feature films and 25 performances in 11 award categories. “Clarissa” and “The Invite” were also nominated for best feature, alongside “Club Kid,” “The Debut,” “Dreams in Nightmares,” “Josephine,” “Mouse,” “Paper Tiger,” “Primetime,” “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma” and “Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother.” Related Stories Inde Navarrette Takes Swipe at Shane Gillis During ‘SNL’ Monologue 'SNL' Sets Druski as First Online Content Creator to Host

“It’s a pleasure to announce this year’s nominees. It has been a remarkable year for film, with audiences turning out in theaters for bold, distinctive work from first-time filmmakers and established artists alike,” said Jeffrey Sharp, executive director of The Gotham Film & Media Institute, announcing the nods. “This year’s nominations, alongside our Tributes and the return of the Audience Award, reflect that abundance and celebrate the creative community that has been at the heart of The Gothams for more than three decades.”
The Gotham Audience Award returns after a six-year hiatus, with this year’s nominees curated from films submitted for consideration and, per a release, “measured by opening-weekend per-theater average against the highest-rated and most-watched films of 2026, as reported in box office tracking and on Letterboxd. The nominees are “Backrooms,” “La Bola Negra,” “The Drama,” “The Invite,” “Michael,” “Obsession,” “Project Hail Mary” and “You Can See Everything.” Gotham members will vote on the winner, and the award will be presented to the film’s credited director (or directors) and producers.
